audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Akshan levels 1, 2 and 3 outright and calls the rest Skill. Every prose string says the opposite: early opens 'Level 1 is his', whys[0] gives level 1 to Ziggs, whys[1] calls level 2 even, spikes[1] says level 6 is 'His spike, not yours', and spikes[3] is titled 'His window all game'. The 43.75% win rate over 16 games agrees with the prose, not the chart.
audit.why: The prose and the win rate point the same way, so the chart is the odd one out — but flipping win[0] from 'Akshan' to 'Ziggs' is a 6-to-5 character change, -16.7%, which the applier's length band rejects, and the same applies to win[1] and win[2]. I did not guess a rewrite of three chart stages. Flagged for the user; the mechanics are corrected regardless.
audit.corrected: NOT APPLIED — raised as a question. The chart's Akshan 1/2/3 contradicts every prose string and the win rate.

audit.why: Akshan's narrow Lvl 3 swing window, Ziggs' Lvl 6, the Youmuu's forcing window, and Ziggs' artillery scaling. Four spikes, correctly owned — this entry is honest that most of them belong to Ziggs.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says twice that 'his Q bomb out-ranges your Q boomerang'. Bouncing Bomb is 850 and Avengerang is 850 — identical — and Avengerang EXTENDS its range each time it hits an enemy, so Akshan's actually reaches further through a wave. It also calls Satchel Charge a blink twice ('W-blinks behind a wall'); it is a self-knockback, not a blink. And Short Fuse is absent entirely, which is the ability that explains why he out-tempos you.
audit.why: Riot's text for Bouncing Bomb: range 850, 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s. Riot's text for Avengerang: range 850, 'extending its range each time it hits an enemy'. Riot's text for Satchel Charge: 'The explosion deals magic damage to enemies, knocking them away. Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage.' Riot's text for Short Fuse: 'Periodically, Ziggs' next basic attack deals bonus magic damage. This cooldown is reduced whenever Ziggs uses an ability.' The reader was told to concede a range war that is actually even, and given the wrong reason for losing it — the real edge is tempo, because every Q he casts pulls his empowered auto forward.
audit.corrected: Bouncing Bomb and Avengerang are both 850, and Avengerang extends through a wave. What beats you is tempo: Q every 6s at rank 1, with Short Fuse's cooldown shortened by every ability cast. Satchel Charge (W, 20s, 1000 range) displaces him, it is not a blink.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge and Hexplosive Minefield are each cited four or five times as the reason your gap-close fails, with no cooldowns anywhere.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 and Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s. Those are the two windows in which Heroic Swing actually works, and the entry's whole thesis is 'find the moment to swing in' — without the numbers there is no moment to find.

audit.whatIsWrong: The minefield's diminishing-returns rule is absent, as is Satchel Charge's max-health component.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage.' That inverts the instinct — edging into a minefield repeatedly is worse than crossing it once, committed, because the first detonation is the expensive one. And Satchel Charge is flagged percent-max-health, so buying durability against him is the wrong reflex.

edits.before: Level 1 is his: his Q bomb out-ranges your Q boomerang and he chips you off the wave for free while you have only your passive's single second shot to answer. Your one trick is E at level 3 — find a wall and Heroic Swing in past his Q arc so you land next to him, then unload your double-shot passive and a point-blank Q before he can satchel you away. Do not walk straight at him to last-hit; eat caster minions with Q from max range and respect that his E minefield will be sitting on the brush you want to swing through.
edits.after: Level 1 is his, but not on range: Bouncing Bomb is 850, the same as Avengerang, and yours EXTENDS with every enemy it clips. What beats you is tempo — his Q refires every 6s and Short Fuse (P) pulls his empowered auto forward with each ability he casts. Your one trick is E at level 3: find a wall, Heroic Swing past his Q arc, then unload the double-shot and a point-blank Q before he satchels you away. Don't walk up to last-hit, and expect Hexplosive Minefield on the brush you want to swing through.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are where the lane gets ugly: he has Q poke, E minefield, and W satchel to wall off every approach, and your Heroic Swing is your only way in — if his Satchel is up he knocks you out of the swing mid-air. At 6 his R is a screen-wide bomb he fires from fog to chunk you, while your R is a weak answer here because the lock-on telegraphs and he just W-blinks behind a wall to break line of sight before your bullets land. Your real value now is leaving: pop W camouflage along terrain and roam mid or bot, where a kill drops your E to a 0.5s cooldown and you can actually snowball something you'll never get standing in this lane.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 get ugly: Q poke, Hexplosive Minefield and Satchel Charge wall off every approach, and Heroic Swing is your only way in — while his 20s Satchel is up, he answers it. One thing helps: successive mine detonations on the SAME target deal reduced damage, so if you must cross the field, cross once and committed rather than edging in and out. At 6 his R fires 5000 units from fog while yours is blunted by the telegraph. Your real value is leaving: pop W camouflage along terrain and roam, where a kill drops E to 0.5s and you snowball something you'll never get in this lane.

edits.before: This is lost if it goes long. Two items of artillery AP and he sieges you and your tower off the map from a range your Q will never touch, dropping E minefields on your approach and W-knocking you out of every Heroic Swing attempt. Your lethality burst falls off hard at 2+ items — you stop one-shotting and he doesn't. Your only path is to have already converted your Youmuu's spike into a lead on a different part of the map; if it's even at 20 minutes, you've lost the lane, so group, use W camouflage to flank, and R-snipe him before he can free-fire bombs into your team from the back line.
edits.after: This is lost if it goes long. Two items of artillery AP and he sieges you and your tower off the map, dropping minefields on your approach and knocking you out of every Heroic Swing attempt — and Satchel Charge bills a share of your MAX health, so durability is not the answer either. Your path is to have already turned the Youmuu's spike into a lead elsewhere on the map; if it's even at 20 minutes you've lost the lane, so group, flank with W camouflage, and R-snipe him off the back line.

edits.after: Bouncing Bomb matches your 850 and refires every 6s, and Short Fuse (P) resets faster with every cast — he out-tempos you, not out-ranges you.

notes: The entry's founding claim was wrong: Bouncing Bomb does not out-range Avengerang. Both are 850, and Avengerang extends its range through every enemy it clips, so Akshan's actually reaches further across a wave. What Ziggs really wins is tempo — Q every 6s at rank 1 with Short Fuse's empowered auto pulled forward by each cast — and Short Fuse was not mentioned anywhere on the page. Conceding a range war you are not losing changes how the whole lane is played. Also corrected Satchel Charge from a 'blink' to a self-knockback, added the 20s and 16s cooldowns that make 'find the window to swing in' actionable, and added the minefield's diminishing-returns rule, which reverses the instinct to edge in and out of it.
unverified: The entry asserts in four places that Satchel Charge knocks Akshan out of Heroic Swing mid-air. Riot's text for Heroic Swing states only that he 'gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain' — whether an external knockback also interrupts the swing is not stated anywhere in champ-data, and akshan.json's needsResearch block is empty. I left the existing claim in place but did not strengthen or repeat it in new text; it needs a wiki check.
